#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcost">LLMRequestCost</a>



**Appears in:**
- [AIGatewayRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aigatewayroutespec)
- [GatewayConfigSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigspec)

LLMRequestCost configures each request cost.

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadataKey` | string | Yes |  | MetadataKey is the key of the metadata to store this cost of the request. |
| `type` | [LLMRequestCostType](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcosttype) | Yes |  | Type specifies the type of the request cost. The default is "OutputToken",<br />and it uses "output token" as the cost. The other types are "InputToken", "TotalToken",<br />"CachedInputToken", "CacheCreationInputToken", "ReasoningToken", and "CEL". |
| `cel` | string | No |  | CEL is the CEL expression to calculate the cost of the request.<br />The CEL expression must return a signed or unsigned integer. If the<br />return value is negative, it will be error.<br />The expression can use the following variables:<br />	* model: the model name extracted from the request content. Type: string.<br />	* backend: the backend name in the form of "name.namespace". Type: string.<br />	* input_tokens: the number of input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />	* cached_input_tokens: the number of cached read input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />	* cache_creation_input_tokens: the number of cache creation input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />	* output_tokens: the number of output tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />	* total_tokens: the total number of tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />	* reasoning_tokens: the number of reasoning tokens. Type: unsigned integer.<br />For example, the following expressions are valid:<br />	* "model == 'llama' ?  input_tokens + output_token * 0.5 : total_tokens"<br />	* "backend == 'foo.default' ?  input_tokens + output_tokens : total_tokens"<br />	* "backend == 'bar.default' ?  (input_tokens - cached_input_tokens) + cached_input_tokens * 0.1 + cache_creation_input_tokens * 1.25 + output_tokens : total_tokens"<br />	* "input_tokens + output_tokens + total_tokens"<br />	* "input_tokens * output_tokens" |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcosttype">LLMRequestCostType</a>

**Underlying type:** string

LLMRequestCostType specifies the type of the LLMRequestCost.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `InputToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeInputToken is the cost type of the input token.<br /> |
| `CachedInputToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeCachedInputToken is the cost type of the cached input token.<br /> |
| `CacheCreationInputToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeCacheCreationInputToken is the cost type of the cached input token.<br /> |
| `OutputToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeOutputToken is the cost type of the output token.<br /> |
| `TotalToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeTotalToken is the cost type of the total token.<br /> |
| `ReasoningToken` | LLMRequestCostTypeReasoningToken is the cost type of the reasoning token.<br /> |
| `CEL` | LLMRequestCostTypeCEL is for calculating the cost using the CEL expression.<br /> |

MCPBackendAPIKey defines the configuration for the API Key Authentication to a backend.
When both `header` and `queryParam` are unspecified, the API key will be injected into the "Authorization" header by default.

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secretRef` | [SecretObjectReference](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/references/spec/#gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1.SecretObjectReference) | No |  | secretRef is the Kubernetes secret which contains the API keys.<br />The key of the secret should be "apiKey". |
| `inline` | string | No |  | Inline contains the API key as an inline string. |
| `header` | string | No |  | Header is the HTTP header to inject the API key into. If not specified,<br />defaults to "Authorization".<br />When the header is "Authorization", the injected header value will be<br />prefixed with "Bearer ".<br />Either one of Header or QueryParam can be specified to inject the API key. |
| `queryParam` | string | No |  | QueryParam is the HTTP query parameter to inject the API key into.<br />For example, if QueryParam is set to "api_key", and the API key is "mysecretkey", the request URL will be modified to include<br />"?api_key=mysecretkey".<br />Either one of Header or QueryParam can be specified to inject the API key.<br />Note: Embedding credentials in URLs (including query parameters) is generally not recommended because URLs can be exposed in logs<br />and intermediary systems; prefer header-based injection when possible. |
| `injectionPolicy` | [MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendapikeyinjectionpolicy) | No | `Always` | InjectionPolicy controls when the configured API key is written onto the target header.<br />Always (the default) writes the credential, replacing any existing value, including<br />values populated by forwardHeaders.<br />IfNotPresent writes the API key only if the target header is absent, so a<br />caller-supplied token forwarded onto the same header is preserved.<br />InjectionPolicy applies only to header injection. It must not be set to IfNotPresent<br />when queryParam is used, because query-parameter injection always rewrites the backend URL. |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendselectorrule">MCPBackendSelectorRule</a>

It does not parse a list of backends<br />out of the request. Each evaluation binds request.mcp.backend to the name of the<br />one candidate backend under test, so the expression should answer "is this backend<br />allowed", not "which backends should be used". A<br />match means the rule applies, and Action below decides whether that's an Allow or<br />a Deny for that backend.<br />Example CEL expressions:<br />	* `request.mcp.backend in request.auth.jwt.claims.mcp_backends`<br />	* `("," + request.headers["x-ai-eg-mcp-backend-subset"] + ",").contains("," + request.mcp.backend + ",")`<br />Available attributes are the same as documented on MCPRouteAuthorizationRule.CEL,<br />except request.mcp.method, request.mcp.tool, and request.mcp.params are not<br />populated (no MCP method has been selected yet at backend-selection time).<br />Note: The CEL expression support is experimental, and the attributes<br />available to the expression may change in future releases. |
| `action` | [AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction) | No | `Allow` | Action is the decision for matching backends. If unspecified, defaults to Allow. |

MCPPromptFilter filters prompts using include and exclude patterns with exact matches or regular expressions.
Exclude rules take precedence over include rules (deny-wins). When both include and exclude are specified,
a prompt must match an include rule AND not match any exclude rule to be allowed.

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

**Appears in:**

MCPRouteAuthorizationRule defines an authorization rule for MCPRoute based on the MCP authorization spec.

| `cel` | string | No |  | CEL specifies a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression evaluated for this rule.<br />The expression must return a boolean; evaluation errors or non-boolean results<br />are treated as "no match".<br />Example CEL expressions:<br />	* `request.method == "POST"`<br />	* `request.headers["x-custom-header"] == "AllowedValue"`<br />	* `request.mcp.tool in ["toolA", "toolB"]`<br />Available attributes in the CEL expression:<br />	* request.method: HTTP method such as GET or POST. Type: string.<br />	* request.headers: map of headers with lowercased keys, first value only. Type: map[string]string.<br />	* request.headers_all: map of headers with lowercased keys, all values. Type: map[string][]string.<br />	* request.path: request path such as /mcp. Type: string.<br />	* request.auth.jwt.claims: JWT claims when a bearer JWT is present. Type: map[string]any.<br />	* request.auth.jwt.scopes: JWT scopes when a bearer JWT is present. Type: []string.<br />	* request.mcp.method: MCP method such as tools/list or tools/call. Type: string.<br />	* request.mcp.backend: upstream backend name (for example, "kiwi" or "github"). Type: string.<br />	* request.mcp.tool: tool name without backend prefix (for example, "list_issues"). Type: string.<br />	* request.mcp.params: parameters of the MCP method, including keys like "_meta" and "arguments". Type: object.<br />Note: The CEL expression support is experimental, and the attributes<br />available to the expression may change in future releases. |
| `action` | [AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction) | No | `Allow` | Action is the authorization decision for matching requests. If unspecified, defaults to Allow. |

MCPRouteOAuth defines a MCP spec compatible OAuth authentication configuration for a MCPRoute.

##### Fields

When set, it replaces the well-known<br />URIs derived from Issuer.<br />Set this when the metadata lives somewhere the issuer does not lead to, for example an issuer<br />of "https://example.com/api/idp/authn" whose document is served only at<br />"https://example.com/api/idp/v4/authn/.well-known/openid-configuration".<br />Issuer is unaffected by this field. It continues to identify the authorization server in the<br />protected resource metadata the gateway publishes, and to derive the well-known URIs when this<br />field is unset. When JWKS is not set, the JWKS URI is discovered from the document fetched here. |

| `claimToHeaders` | ClaimToHeader array | No |  | ClaimToHeaders specifies JWT claims to extract and forward as HTTP headers to backend MCP servers.<br />This enables backends to access user identity for authorization, auditing, or personalization.<br />Security considerations:<br />- Any client-provided headers matching the configured header names will be stripped to prevent forgery<br />- Only the specified claims are extracted; the full JWT is not forwarded to backends<br />- Consider using a header prefix (e.g., "X-Jwt-Claim-") to avoid conflicts with other headers |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteprefixmode">MCPRoutePrefixMode</a>

**Underlying type:** string

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPRoutePrefixMode controls how tool and prompt names are prefixed when exposed to clients.

PrefixMode can be set at the route level (MCPRouteSpec) and overridden per backend
(MCPRouteBackendRef); the per-backend value takes precedence when set. A single route can
therefore mix Always and Never backends. This is intentional: it lets an operator keep the
route-level default (Always is recommended for most routes, since it guarantees a collision-free
catalog without any extra configuration) while opting specific, well-known backends into bare
names, e.g. to match tool names an existing client or interactive MCP App already hardcodes.
Per-backend override is meant as a targeted escape hatch, not a replacement for choosing one
naming policy for the route as a whole.


##### Possible Values

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Always` | MCPRoutePrefixModeAlways prefixes tool/prompt names with `<backendName>__`.<br />This is the default and preserves existing behavior.<br /> |
| `Never` | MCPRoutePrefixModeNever exposes tool/prompt names unprefixed.<br />Tool names must be unique across all Never-mode backends on the route.<br /> |

In other words, the Gateway resources must be in the<br />same namespace as the MCPRoute. Currently, each reference's Kind must be Gateway. |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-openaisubjecttoken">OpenAISubjectToken</a>



**Appears in:**
- [OpenAIWorkloadIdentityFederationConfig](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-openaiworkloadidentityfederationconfig)

OpenAISubjectToken specifies the source of the subject token exchanged for an OpenAI access token.
Exactly one source must be configured.

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oidcExchangeToken` | [BackendSecurityPolicyOIDC](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-backendsecuritypolicyoidc) | No |  | OIDCExchangeToken obtains the subject token from an OIDC provider via the client-credentials flow.<br />The OIDC provider must return a JWT access token. |
| `spiffeJWTSVID` | [BackendSecurityPolicySPIFFEJWTSVID](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-backendsecuritypolicyspiffejwtsvid) | No |  | SPIFFEJWTSVID obtains the subject token as a JWT-SVID from the SPIFFE Workload API.<br />The SPIFFE identity is owned by the controller, not by the policy: the JWT-SVID is issued for the<br />controller's SPIFFE ID. This differs from OIDCExchangeToken, where the policy supplies its own<br />credentials. Every policy using this source authenticates as the controller and can obtain access<br />tokens for any OpenAI service account mapped to the controller's SPIFFE ID, so only trusted cluster<br />admins should be allowed to create such policies. |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-openaiworkloadidentityfederationconfig">OpenAIWorkloadIdentityFederationConfig</a>



**Appears in:**
- [BackendSecurityPolicyOpenAICredentials](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-backendsecuritypolicyopenaicredentials)

OpenAIWorkloadIdentityFederationConfig specifies how the controller obtains an OpenAI access token via
OpenAI Workload Identity Federation. The controller obtains a subject token, exchanges it at
https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token for a short-lived OpenAI access token, and stores the access token in a secret, rotating it before it expires.

The identity provider and service account mapping must be configured in the OpenAI organization, with the
issuer and audience of the subject token.

https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/workload-identity-federation

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `identityProviderID` | string | Yes |  | IdentityProviderID is the ID of the OpenAI Workload Identity Provider configured for the issuer of the<br />subject token, e.g. "idp_abc123". |
| `serviceAccountID` | string | Yes |  | ServiceAccountID is the ID of the OpenAI service account the access token is issued for. It must match a<br />service account mapping of the identity provider. |
| `subjectToken` | [OpenAISubjectToken](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-openaisubjecttoken) | Yes |  | SubjectToken specifies where the subject token is obtained from. The subject token must be a JWT. |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-protectedresourcemetadata">ProtectedResourceMetadata</a>



**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteOAuth](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteoauth)

ProtectedResourceMetadata represents the Protected Resource Metadata	of the MCP server as per RFC 9728.

References:
* https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization#authorization-server-location
* https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728#name-protected-resource-metadata

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | string | No |  | Resource is the identifier of the protected resource.<br />This should match the MCPRoute's URL. For example, if the MCPRoute's URL is<br />"https://api.example.com/mcp", the Resource should be "https://api.example.com/mcp".<br />When omitted, the gateway derives the resource identifier per request from the<br />scheme, authority and path the client actually used to reach the MCP endpoint.<br />Leave it unset unless the gateway is fronted by something that rewrites the<br />externally visible URL in a way the forwarded headers do not reflect.<br />The derived identifier names the request's Host. Set Hostnames to restrict which hosts<br />it can name: the metadata endpoint is only reachable on hosts Hostnames matches. Without<br />Hostnames, every authority the Gateway listener accepts is reflected as-is.<br />Audiences need not be the resource URL; it is whatever the authorization server puts in<br />the token's "aud". Only an authorization server that honours RFC 8707 binds "aud" to the<br />"resource" parameter, which clients set to the advertised identifier. With such a server<br />and a non-empty Audiences, a derived identifier has to agree with Audiences, so list every<br />address the route is reachable on, or set Resource explicitly. |
| `resourceName` | string | No |  | ResourceName is a human-readable name for the protected resource. |
| `scopesSupported` | string array | No |  | ScopesSupported defines the minimal set of scopes required for the basic functionality of the MCPRoute.<br />It should avoid broad or overly permissive scopes to prevent clients from requesting tokens with excessive privileges.<br />If an operation requires additional scopes that are not present in the access token, the client will receive a<br />403 Forbidden response that includes the required scopes in the `scope` field of the `WWW-Authenticate` header.<br />This enables incremental privilege elevation through targeted `WWW-Authenticate: scope="..."` challenges when<br />privileged operations are first attempted. |
| `resourceSigningAlgValuesSupported` | string array | No |  | ResourceSigningAlgValuesSupported is a list of JWS signing algorithms supported by the resource server.<br />These algorithms are used in the "alg" field of the JOSE header in signed tokens. |
| `resourceDocumentation` | string | No |  | ResourceDocumentation is a URL that provides human-readable documentation for the resource. |
| `resourcePolicyUri` | string | No |  | ResourcePolicyURI is a URL that points to the resource server's policy document. |

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-toolcall">ToolCall</a>

#### <a name="github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-versionedapischema">VersionedAPISchema</a>



**Appears in:**
- [AIServiceBackendSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aiservicebackendspec)

VersionedAPISchema defines the API schema of either AIGatewayRoute (the input) or AIServiceBackend (the output).

This allows the ai-gateway to understand the input and perform the necessary transformation
depending on the API schema pair (input, output).

Note that this is vendor specific, and the stability of the API schema is not guaranteed by
the ai-gateway, but by the vendor via proper versioning.

##### Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [APISchema](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-apischema) | Yes |  | Name is the name of the API schema of the AIGatewayRoute or AIServiceBackend. |
| `version` | string | No |  | Version is the version of the API schema.<br />When the name is set to AzureOpenAI, this version maps to "API Version" in the<br />Azure OpenAI API documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/reference#rest-api-versioning).<br />This field is ignored for OpenAI, AWSBedrock, GCPVertexAI, and Anthropic.<br />For OpenAI and Anthropic, use prefix to configure custom request paths.<br />See https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/capabilities/llm-integrations/supported-providers for details. |
| `prefix` | string | No |  | Prefix is the prefix for the API.<br />When the name is set to "OpenAI", "chat completions" API endpoint will be "$\{this_field\}/chat/completions".<br />When the name is set to "Anthropic", the "messages" API endpoint will be "$\{this_field\}/messages".<br />It can be with or without a leading slash ("/").<br />This field is ignored for AWSAnthropic and GCPAnthropic.<br />This is especially useful when routing to a backend that has an OpenAI or Anthropic compatible API but has a different<br />prefix. For example, Gemini OpenAI compatible API (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai) uses<br />"/v1beta/openai" prefix. Another example is that Cohere AI (https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/compatibility-api)<br />uses "/compatibility/v1" prefix. On the other hand, DeepSeek (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/) doesn't<br />use prefix, so you can leave this field unset.<br />See https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/capabilities/llm-integrations/supported-providers for details. |
